stories.headline: Amazon Invests Up to $25B in Anthropic, Secures $100B+ AWS Compute Commitment Over 10 Years

key_facts.fact: Amazon will invest $5 billion in Anthropic immediately, with up to $20 billion more tied to commercial milestones, on top of $8 billion already invested — bringing total potential investment to ~$33 billion.
key_facts.excerpt: Amazon to invest $5 billion in Anthropic today and up to an additional $20 billion in the future. This is in addition to the $8 billion Amazon previously invested in Anthropic.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic commits to spending more than $100 billion on AWS technologies over the next 10 years, including current and future generations of Trainium chips (Trainium2 through Trainium4) and tens of millions of Graviton CPU cores.
key_facts.excerpt: Anthropic to spend more than $100 billion over the next ten years on AWS technologies. This encompasses current and future generations of Trainium and tens of millions of Graviton cores.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic secures up to 5 gigawatts of compute capacity, with nearly 1 GW of combined Trainium2 and Trainium3 capacity expected online by end of 2026.

key_facts.fact: Anthropic's annualized revenue has reached $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at end of 2025.
key_facts.excerpt: the company's annualised revenue has reached $30 billion, up from approximately $9 billion at the end of 2025.

key_facts.fact: The deal follows Amazon's $50 billion investment in OpenAI announced two months earlier, making Amazon the largest investor in both leading AI labs.

stories.headline: Apple Names Johny Srouji Chief Hardware Officer, Reorganizes Hardware Into Five Groups

key_facts.fact: Apple promoted Johny Srouji to the newly created role of Chief Hardware Officer, effective April 20, combining hardware engineering and hardware technologies divisions under one organization.
key_facts.excerpt: Apple today announced that, effective immediately, Apple executive Johny Srouji will become chief hardware officer.

key_facts.fact: Srouji organized the combined division into five areas: hardware engineering (Tom Marieb, ex-Intel), silicon (Sri Santhanam, 18-year veteran), advanced technologies (Zongjian Chen), platform architecture (Tim Millet, 21-year veteran), and program management (Donny Nordhues).
key_facts.excerpt: Srouji will organize the combined hardware engineering and hardware technologies group into five areas: Hardware engineering: Overseen by Tom Marieb... Silicon: Overseen by Sri Santhanam... Advanced technologies: Overseen by Zongjian Chen... Platform architecture: Overseen by Tim Millet... Project management: Overseen by Donny Nordhues.

key_facts.fact: The restructuring accompanies the announcement that John Ternus will succeed Tim Cook as Apple CEO on September 1, with Cook becoming executive chairman.
key_facts.excerpt: As part of Apple's reorganization elevating John Ternus to CEO, the company also promoted Johny Srouji to a broader new chief hardware officer role.

key_facts.fact: Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of the A4, Apple's first custom system-on-a-chip, after senior positions at Intel and IBM in processor design.
key_facts.excerpt: Srouji joined Apple in 2008 to lead development of A4, the first Apple-designed system-on-a-chip. Prior to Apple, Srouji held senior positions at Intel and IBM in the area of processor development and design.

key_facts.fact: The reorganization returns Apple to an earlier model used under former hardware chief Bob Mansfield, when hardware operated as a single unit; it was later split, allowing Ternus and Srouji to rise through separate divisions.
key_facts.excerpt: The move marks a return to an earlier organizational model used more than a decade ago, when Apple's hardware teams operated as a single unit under former hardware chief Bob Mansfield.

stories.headline: BMW Expands Humanoid Robot Program to German EV Factory After Building 30K+ Vehicles in US Pilot

key_facts.fact: BMW is deploying Hexagon Robotics' AEON humanoid robots at its Leipzig, Germany factory for EV production, after a successful pilot at its Spartanburg, South Carolina plant.
key_facts.excerpt: After a successful pilot in Spartanburg, South Carolina, BMW is bringing that same idea into its Leipzig, Germany, factory, where it is testing robots in real production environments. This time, it is partnering with Hexagon Robotics to introduce a new generation of AI-powered machines.

key_facts.fact: BMW's earlier pilot used Figure 02 humanoid robots for precise sheet metal positioning on the X3 production line, contributing to building more than 30,000 vehicles.
key_facts.excerpt: BMW's earlier pilot used Figure 02 humanoid robots for a very specific task. They handled the precise positioning of sheet metal for welding on the BMW X3 production line... According to BMW, those robots helped contribute to building more than 30,000 vehicles.

key_facts.fact: The AEON robots use AI-based motion control and real-time sensors to adapt to their environment without constant human direction, which Hexagon calls 'Physical AI.'
key_facts.excerpt: They rely on AI-based motion control, which helps them move through complex spaces. At the same time, built-in sensors allow them to understand their surroundings in real time... Hexagon refers to this as 'Physical AI.'

key_facts.fact: BMW executive Michael Nikolaides framed the deployment as part of the company's broader iFACTORY initiative for digitalization and production competitiveness.
key_facts.excerpt: Michael Nikolaides, who oversees BMW's production network, says these pilot programs help the company refine how AI-powered robots learn on the job... 'Digitalization improves the competitiveness... opens up entirely new possibilities in production.'

stories.headline: CFIUS Blocks Chinese LED Maker Sanan's $239M Acquisition of Dutch Firm Lumileds

key_facts.fact: China's leading LED chipmaker Sanan Optoelectronics and its Malaysian partner withdrew their US$239 million all-cash offer to acquire Lumileds Holding after CFIUS concluded the deal posed 'irresolvable U.S. national security risks.'
key_facts.excerpt: CFIUS concluded the deal would pose 'irresolvable U.S. national security risks' and requested that the parties withdraw their application and terminate the transaction.

key_facts.fact: No equity transfer payment had been made and the target shares had not been delivered; Sanan said the termination will not materially affect its operations or financial position.
key_facts.excerpt: As of the transaction's termination, no equity transfer payment had been made and the target shares had not been delivered or settled. Sanan Optoelectronics stated in its announcement that the termination does not trigger any breach of contract.

key_facts.fact: Lumileds ranks third globally in automotive lighting LED revenue behind ams OSRAM and Nichia, and is part of Apple's smartphone flash LED supply chain.
key_facts.excerpt: It ranks third globally in automotive lighting LED revenue, behind only ams OSRAM and Nichia. In smartphone flash LEDs, it is part of Apple's supply chain, ranking just below Nichia.

key_facts.fact: Sanan had planned to use Lumileds' manufacturing facilities in Singapore and Malaysia to strengthen its overseas production capacity and global customer supply.
key_facts.excerpt: The move was aimed at quickly securing overseas production capacity and strengthening supply for global customers by leveraging Lumileds' manufacturing facilities in Singapore and Malaysia.

stories.headline: Renewables Overtake Coal in Global Power Generation for First Time in Over a Century

key_facts.fact: Clean electricity met all growth in global power demand in 2025 (887 TWh vs 849 TWh demand growth), keeping fossil fuel generation flat for the first time this century, per Ember's Global Electricity Review 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: Clean generation rose by 887 TWh, slightly exceeding demand growth of 849 TWh, resulting in a 0.2 per cent decline in fossil fuel-based generation.

key_facts.fact: Renewables reached nearly 34% of global electricity generation, overtaking coal's 33% share for the first time in over a century; coal power dropped by 63 TWh (-0.6%).
key_facts.excerpt: This shift pushed renewables to nearly 34 per cent of global electricity generation, overtaking coal's 33 per cent share for the first time in over a century.

key_facts.fact: Solar generation rose 30% in 2025 (636 TWh increase), the fastest growth rate in eight years; solar alone met 75% of global electricity demand growth, while solar and wind together met 99%.
key_facts.excerpt: Solar, which grew 30% in 2025, alone met three-quarters of last year's net rise in electricity demand — and combined with wind power generation, met 99% of it.

key_facts.fact: Battery storage grew 46% in 2025 as costs fell 45%; enough capacity was added to shift 14% of solar generation to times when the sun isn't shining.
key_facts.excerpt: As battery costs fell 45% last year, storage grew 46% in 2025. Ember estimates that enough battery capacity was added last year to shift 14% of the solar generation.

key_facts.fact: Global emissions intensity fell to 458 gCO2e per kWh in 2025, down 2.7% from 2024 and down 16% from 2005.
key_facts.excerpt: In 2025, the average kilowatt hour produced globally resulted in emissions of 458 gCO2e, 2.7 per cent less than in 2024 (471 gCO2e) and down 16 per cent from two decades ago in 2005.

stories.headline: EU to Unblock €90B Ukraine Loan on Wednesday as Orbán Lifts Blockade

key_facts.fact: EU countries will on Wednesday unblock a €90 billion loan to Ukraine, approved in December to cover Kyiv's military and financial needs through 2027, after outgoing Hungarian PM Viktor Orbán lifted his blockade.
key_facts.excerpt: The European Union will unblock a €90 billion loan to Ukraine on Wednesday. In December the EU approved the loan, meeting Kyiv's military and financial needs through 2027. However, Hungary and its pro-Kremlin Prime Minister Viktor Orbán held up implementation.

key_facts.fact: The blockade was removed after April 12 Hungarian elections ended Orbán's 16-year rule; incoming PM Péter Magyar promised smoother EU relations and criticized Orbán for bowing to Russian influence.
key_facts.excerpt: The now-caretaker Hungarian prime minister, friendly to Vladimir Putin, had been blocking the loan but will soon be replaced by Peter Magyar, who won a sweeping electoral mandate. Magyar has promised smoother relations with Brussels and criticised Orbán for bowing to Russian influence.

key_facts.fact: Ukraine will resume transit of Russian oil to Hungary via the Druzhba pipeline on April 21 at noon as part of the deal; deliveries had been stopped since January 21.
key_facts.excerpt: Ukraine will resume oil transit from Russia to Hungary via the Druzhba pipeline on April 21 at noon. The MOL Group, which purchases Russian oil for its refineries in Hungary and Slovakia, has recently been using raw material from Hungarian state strategic reserves. Deliveries via Druzhba have been stopped since January 21.

key_facts.fact: French President Macron said with Orbán's departure, 'we can be reasonably optimistic about the sound progress and implementation' of the EU loan.
key_facts.excerpt: French President Emmanuel Macron assured, 'We can be reasonably optimistic about the sound progress.'

key_facts.fact: Germany summoned the Russian Ambassador on Monday over 'direct threats from Russia' against targets in Germany; Russia's Defense Ministry had named three German firms supplying drones to Ukraine.
key_facts.excerpt: The German Foreign Ministry summoned the Russian Ambassador on Monday over 'direct threats from Russia' against 'targets in Germany'. Russia's Defense Ministry suggested last week that at least three German firms could be targeted for supplying drones to Ukraine.

stories.headline: FDA Accepts Roche's Gazyva Filing for Lupus, Potential First Anti-CD20 Therapy for SLE

key_facts.fact: The FDA accepted Roche's supplemental Biologics License Application (sBLA) for Gazyva/Gazyvaro (obinutuzumab) for systemic lupus erythematosus (SLE); a decision is expected by December 2026.
key_facts.excerpt: The FDA is expected to make a decision on an approval by December 2026. Gazyva/Gazyvaro is already approved for adults with lupus nephritis in the US and EU.

key_facts.fact: If approved, Gazyva would be the first anti-CD20 therapy to directly target B cells in SLE, potentially becoming the new standard of care for a disease affecting more than 3 million people worldwide.
key_facts.excerpt: If approved, Gazyva/Gazyvaro would be the first anti-CD20 therapy to directly target B cells in SLE, potentially becoming the new standard of care for this condition.

key_facts.fact: Phase III ALLEGORY results showed 76.7% of patients on Gazyva plus standard therapy achieved SRI-4 response at 52 weeks vs 53.5% on placebo (adjusted difference 23.1%, p<0.001); the remission rate more than doubled (33.8% vs 13.8%).
key_facts.excerpt: Over three quarters (76.7%) of people treated with Gazyva/Gazyvaro plus standard therapy achieved a minimum four-point improvement in SRI-4 at 52 weeks, compared to 53.5% with placebo plus standard therapy (adjusted difference 23.1%, 95% CI: 12.5-33.6, p<0.001).

key_facts.fact: Gazyva-treated patients were significantly less likely to have disease flares through 52 weeks (HR 0.58, p=0.002) and had lower steroid dependence, with the glucocorticoid dose sustained at ≤7.5 mg/day from week 40 to 52.
key_facts.excerpt: The study showed that people receiving Gazyva/Gazyvaro, plus standard therapy, were less likely to have a flare through to week 52 (Hazard ratio: 0.58, 95% CI: 0.40-0.82, p=0.002).

key_facts.excerpt: New sign-ups are paused for GitHub Copilot Pro, Pro+, and Student plans. GitHub states this allows them to serve existing customers more effectively.

key_facts.fact: Opus models removed from Pro plans entirely; Opus 4.7 remains available on Pro+ only. Opus 4.5 and 4.6 being removed from Pro+ as previously announced.

key_facts.fact: Usage limits tightened for individual plans, with Pro+ now offering more than 5× the limits of Pro. Two types of limits: session limits (prevent peak overload) and weekly token-consumption caps.
key_facts.excerpt: Usage limits are being tightened for individual plans. Pro+ plans now offer more than 5X the limits of Pro plans.

key_facts.fact: GitHub is offering refunds for Pro or Pro+ subscriptions canceled between April 20 and May 20, 2026, acknowledging the changes are disruptive.
key_facts.excerpt: GitHub acknowledges these changes are disruptive and is offering refunds for Pro or Pro+ subscriptions canceled between April 20 and May 20, 2026.

key_facts.fact: Long-running, parallelized agentic sessions now consume far more resources than the original plan structure was built to support, GitHub VP of product Joe Binder said.

stories.headline: Google's Sergey Brin Forms DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' to Close Gap With Anthropic

key_facts.fact: Google co-founder Sergey Brin is personally leading a new DeepMind 'Coding Strike Team' aimed at closing Gemini's gap with Anthropic's Claude on code generation, according to The Information.
key_facts.excerpt: Google co-founder Sergey Brin has reportedly urged DeepMind employees to focus on improving AI agents... Google assembles a dedicated team of researchers and engineers to strengthen its AI coding models.

key_facts.fact: In an internal memo, Brin wrote: 'To win the final sprint, we must urgently bridge the gap in agentic execution and turn our models into primary developers.' He framed improving coding as the path to self-improving AI — AI that trains the next AI.
key_facts.excerpt: In the memo, Brin wrote, 'To win the final sprint, we must urgently bridge the gap in agentic execution and turn our models into primary developers' of code. The end goal is AI takeoff, or AI that can improve itself.

key_facts.fact: The strike team is led by research engineer Sebastian Borgeaud, who previously ran DeepMind's pretraining. Both Brin and DeepMind CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu are directly involved.
key_facts.excerpt: Research engineer Sebastian Borgeaud, who previously ran DeepMind's pretraining, is leading the group under CTO Koray Kavukcuoglu and Brin.

key_facts.fact: DeepMind researchers internally rate Claude's code-writing above Gemini's, which drove Brin's push. Google is now training models on its own proprietary codebase rather than public datasets typically used for general-purpose coding agents.
key_facts.excerpt: Researchers at Google DeepMind view Anthropic's coding tools as ahead of the code-writing capabilities of Google's Gemini models. Google is now placing more emphasis on models that write code for internal use, shifting from its earlier focus on tools for external customers.

key_facts.fact: Gemini engineers are now required to use Google's internal agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on a company leaderboard called 'Jetski.'
key_facts.excerpt: Gemini engineers now have to use Google's internal agent tools on complex tasks, with usage tracked on a company leaderboard called Jetski.

stories.headline: Iran-US Ceasefire Expires Wednesday as Both Sides Signal Round 2 Talks in Islamabad

key_facts.excerpt: Trump said this morning that Iran has 'no choice but to send' negotiators to a new round of talks in Pakistan. 'What I think is that we're going to end up with a great deal,' the president told CNBC.

key_facts.fact: Two regional officials told the AP that the US and Iran are signaling they will hold a new round of ceasefire talks in Islamabad, with VP JD Vance and Iran's Qalibaf expected to arrive early Wednesday.

stories.headline: Moonshot AI Releases Kimi K2.6, Open-Weight 1T-Parameter Model Rivaling Frontier Labs on Coding

key_facts.fact: Kimi K2.6 is a 1 trillion total parameter Mixture-of-Experts model with 32 billion active parameters per token, 384 experts (8 routed + 1 shared), 256K context window, and native multimodal input (text, image, video).
key_facts.excerpt: a Mixture-of-Experts system with 1 trillion total parameters and 32 billion active per token. It ships with open weights on Hugging Face under a Modified MIT license, native INT4 quantization, and a 256K context window

key_facts.fact: K2.6 scores 80.2% on SWE-Bench Verified, 58.6% on SWE-Bench Pro (beating Claude Opus 4.6's 53.4% and GPT-5.4's 57.7%), and 54.0% on Humanity's Last Exam with tools (beating GPT-5.4's 52.1%).
key_facts.excerpt: SWE-Bench Verified 80.2%, SWE-Bench Pro 58.6% vs Claude Opus 4.6 53.4%, Humanity's Last Exam (with tools) 54.0% vs GPT-5.4 52.1%

key_facts.fact: The model supports an agent-swarm primitive coordinating up to 300 parallel sub-agents across 4,000 steps per run, and can code continuously for 12+ hours.
key_facts.excerpt: 300 parallel sub-agents, 12-hour autonomous coding sessions

key_facts.fact: K2.6 ranks #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, scoring 54 — just 3 points behind Claude Opus 4.7, Gemini 3.1 Pro, and GPT-5.4, all tied at 57.
key_facts.excerpt: Kimi K2.6 has debuted at #4 on the Artificial Analysis Intelligence Index v4.0, scoring 54 out of a possible index points — just three points behind the trio of Anthropic (Claude Opus 4.7), Google (Gemini 3.1 Pro), and OpenAI (GPT-5.4), all of which are tied at 57.

key_facts.fact: API pricing is $0.60 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens — roughly 10× cheaper than Claude Opus 4.7. Weights available on Hugging Face under Modified MIT License.
key_facts.excerpt: priced at $0.60 per million input tokens and $2.50 per million output tokens through the Kimi API. Claude Opus 4.7 lists at $5 and $25 for the same surfaces.

stories.headline: OpenAI Launches Chronicle for Codex, Building AI Memory From Screen Captures

key_facts.fact: Chronicle is a research preview feature in Codex for macOS that periodically captures screenshots, sends them to OpenAI servers for processing, and stores text summaries as local unencrypted Markdown files to build persistent context.
key_facts.excerpt: Chronicle periodically captures your screen, processes the content into text summaries, and stores those summaries as local memory files that give the AI assistant context about what you have been working on.

key_facts.fact: Available only to ChatGPT Pro subscribers ($100+/month) on Apple Silicon Macs. Not available in the EU, UK, or Switzerland. Requires macOS Screen Recording and Accessibility permissions.
key_facts.excerpt: Chronicle is in an opt-in research preview. It is only available for ChatGPT Pro subscribers on macOS, and is not yet available in the EU, UK and Switzerland.

key_facts.fact: Screen captures are stored temporarily on-device and auto-deleted after 6 hours. OpenAI says screenshots are not stored on servers after processing and are not used for training.
key_facts.excerpt: Screen captures are ephemeral and will only be saved temporarily on your computer. Screen captures that are older than 6 hours will be deleted while Chronicle is running.

key_facts.fact: Chronicle processes screenshots in the cloud, contrasting with Microsoft Recall's on-device approach and drawing comparisons to the now-defunct Rewind AI. OpenAI warns the feature increases risk of prompt injection from screen content.
key_facts.excerpt: Recall takes screenshots and processes them locally using the neural processing unit on the device. No screenshot data leaves the machine. Chronicle takes the opposite approach: processing happens in the cloud.

key_facts.fact: Over one million developers have used Codex, and usage doubled following the GPT-5.2-Codex model launch in December. Chronicle is part of a broader update that added computer use, in-app browser, image generation, and 90+ plugins.

stories.headline: US Space Force Cancels GPS Ground Control System After 16 Years and Nearly $8B

key_facts.fact: The Pentagon canceled the GPS Next-Generation Operational Control System (OCX), ending a 16-year, multibillion-dollar effort to deliver a command and control system for GPS satellites; the decision was made by defense acquisition executive Michael Duffey on April 17.
key_facts.excerpt: The Global Positioning System Next-Generation Operational Control System, known by the acronym OCX, was officially canceled by Michael Duffey, the Pentagon's defense acquisition executive, on Friday, April 17.

key_facts.fact: The OCX contract was awarded to Raytheon (now RTX) in 2010 with a timetable for completion in 2016 at $3.7 billion; budget projections grew to nearly $8 billion — more than double the original cost.
key_facts.excerpt: The Pentagon awarded the OCX contract to Raytheon, now known as RTX Corporation, in 2010, with a timetable for completion in 2016 at a cost of $3.7 billion. Budget projections to finish the program grew to nearly $8 billion.

key_facts.fact: RTX delivered the system to the Space Force in 2025, but further integrated tests revealed it was still not ready; problems were discovered 'across a broad range of capability areas that would put current GPS capabilities at risk.'
key_facts.excerpt: RTX finally delivered the control system to the Space Force last year, but further tests revealed it was still not ready for GPS operations.

key_facts.fact: As of January 2026, costs were estimated at $6.27 billion; the Space Force will instead continue enhancing the existing Architecture Evolution Plan (AEP) control system.
key_facts.excerpt: The service said that as of January 2026 the cost was estimated to be $6.27 billion. Instead, we will continue enhancing the current control system to operate the GPS satellite constellation.

stories.headline: UK Moves to Break Gas-Electricity Price Link, Raises Generator Levy to 55%

key_facts.fact: The UK government announced measures to decouple electricity prices from volatile gas prices, offering voluntary long-term fixed contracts to existing low-carbon generators covering about a third of Britain's power supply.
key_facts.excerpt: Voluntary long term fixed contracts: offered to existing low-carbon generators not on fixed‑price contracts – covering around a third of Britain's power supply.

key_facts.fact: The Electricity Generator Levy rate was raised from 45% to 55% to tax excess profits when gas prices spike, ensuring more windfall revenue reaches households affected by the Iran war energy crisis.
key_facts.excerpt: An updated Electricity Generators Levy: immediate action to tax excess profits through the Electricity Generator Levy by raising the rate from 45% to 55%, ensuring an increased proportion of the extraordinary revenues generated when the gas price spikes is available to government.

key_facts.fact: Gas currently sets the wholesale price of electricity about 60% of the time in Britain, down from 90% in the early 2020s; the government projects this will fall to about 30% by the early 2030s through its clean energy mission.
key_facts.excerpt: Britain has already moved from gas setting the price of electricity around 90% of the time in the early 2020s, to around 60% today. Through the government's clean energy mission, it is estimated gas will set the wholesale price around 30% of the time by the early 2030s.

key_facts.fact: The government is also exploring use of public land to unlock up to 10 GW of renewable capacity, and plans to accelerate 57,000 solar installations for households this year.
key_facts.excerpt: Driving forward plans to massively expand renewables across the Public Estate – including using brownfield land, industrial sites and railway sites to host solar panels and wind turbines. This could unlock up to 10GW of capacity.

key_facts.fact: Victory Giant makes high-end printed circuit boards (PCBs), a crucial component of AI servers, with Nvidia as one of its key customers. The company is already listed in Shenzhen.

stories.headline: Fed Chair Nominee Kevin Warsh Pledges Independence at High-Stakes Senate Hearing

key_facts.fact: Kevin Warsh, Trump's nominee to lead the Federal Reserve, told the Senate Banking Committee he is 'committed to ensuring that the conduct of monetary policy remains strictly independent' in prepared remarks released April 20.
key_facts.excerpt: Kevin Warsh will tell lawmakers at his Senate confirmation hearing on Tuesday that he is 'committed to ensuring that the conduct of monetary policy remains strictly independent.'

key_facts.fact: Warsh qualified his independence pledge, saying Fed independence is 'at its peak in the operational conduct of monetary policy' but does not extend to the same 'special deference' in bank regulation, public monies, or international finance.
key_facts.excerpt: Fed independence is 'at its peak in the operational conduct of monetary policy,' Warsh said. 'That degree of independence does not extend to the full range of its congressionally mandated functions.'

key_facts.fact: Republican Sen. Thom Tillis is effectively blocking a committee vote on Warsh until the DOJ drops its criminal investigation into Fed Chair Jerome Powell over a building renovation; Powell's term as chair ends May 15.
key_facts.excerpt: Sen. Thom Tillis, a North Carolina Republican, has said he would effectively block Warsh until the probe is dropped. Powell's term as chair ends May 15.

key_facts.fact: Warsh would be the wealthiest Fed chair if confirmed, with financial holdings totaling more than $100 million; Democrats signaled they will press him on transparency around those holdings.
key_facts.excerpt: Democrats on the committee have already signaled they will press him about what they argue is a lack of transparency regarding some of his vast financial holdings, which total more than $100 million.

key_facts.fact: The Fed funds rate currently sits at 3.50%-3.75% after the FOMC held steady at its last two meetings; Goldman Sachs expects up to two 25bp rate cuts in 2026 but timing remains uncertain due to Iran war-driven inflation.
key_facts.excerpt: The benchmark Federal Funds Rate is currently 3.50% to 3.75% after the policy-making Federal Open Market Committee held the rate steady after its last two meetings. Goldman said it continues to expect the Fed could deliver as many as two 25 basis point rate cuts in 2026 but that timing remains uncertain.

stories.headline: Wärtsilä Wins 412 MW Gas Engine Order for Off-Grid Ohio Hyperscale Data Center

key_facts.fact: Wärtsilä received an order to supply 412 MW of gas engine power for a major hyperscale data center in Ohio, using 40 Wärtsilä 34SG spark-ignited gas engines.
key_facts.excerpt: Technology group Wärtsilä has received an order to supply 412 MW of engine power to support a major new hyperscale data center project in Ohio, United States. The project includes 40 Wärtsilä 34SG (spark gas) engines.

key_facts.fact: The order brings Wärtsilä's total engine capacity sold into the US data center market to over 1.6 GW; this is the company's fourth US data center order.
key_facts.excerpt: This order brings Wärtsilä's total engine capacity sold into the US data center market to over 1.6 GW... This is Wärtsilä's fourth data center related order in the USA.

key_facts.fact: The power plant will operate off-grid as primary power, enabling the data center to avoid long grid interconnection delays common to the US market, with commercial operation expected by early 2028.
key_facts.excerpt: The power plant will provide highly flexible, primary power, enabling the data center to operate off-grid and avoid long interconnection delays common to the US market. Equipment deliveries are scheduled to align with an anticipated commercial operation date of early 2028.

key_facts.fact: This is the first deployment of Wärtsilä's proven 34SG engine model in a data center application; the modular design scales up to 500MW+.
key_facts.excerpt: This latest order marks the first use of the highly proven 34SG model in a data center application... Its modular design accommodates data center developers looking for power solutions that can be deployed in modular blocks, scaling up to 500MW+.
